newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Bansud in share swap with Banamex.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Bansud in share swap with Banamex.

text.p: Argentina's Bansud, controlled by Mexico's Banamex, said Tuesday its local shareholders decided to swap with the Mexican bank part of Bansud's A shares, which carry five votes, for single-vote B shares.
Shareholders Enrique Jaratz and Rafael Seragopian decided to swap 100 percent of their shares, Bansud told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange in a letter.
In a separate agreement to last until Jan 1, 2002, the banks decided:
* Bansud's local shareholders will be in charge of the bank's administration.

* Both Banamex and the local shareholders commit themselves to act jointly through Bansud or its subsidiaries in any financial venture in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay.
* Local shareholders agree to restrict the tranfer of all their Bansud A shares and a part of their B shares. That restriction can only be lifted with Banamex consent.
Bansud said the capital structure and voting power of Bansud is left as follows:
Local shareholders have a 15.64 percent of the bank's capital and 16.94 percent of the votes.
Banamex has a 56.62 percent of the bank's capital and 69.24 percent of the votes.
Other shareholders have a 27.74 percent of capital and 13.82 percent of votes.
No other details were immediately available.
